c.v: The test case puts both nodes into one executor and spins it until the monitor has heard five heartbeats, or five seconds have passed:
Each line has a reason. One executor runs both nodes' callbacks in the test's own thread, so
is read by the same thread that writes it, and needs no lock.
waits up to 100 ms for one callback to be ready, runs it, and returns, which lets the loop check its two conditions.

would be the wrong choice here: when nothing is ready it returns at once, and the loop would keep a CPU core busy until the deadline. The deadline turns a broken exchange into a failed test instead of a CI job that hangs. The test asks for five heartbeats, not heartbeats 0 to 4, because the first ones can be lost during discovery, as you saw in Build 1.
The two tests split the work.
decides whether the rules are right, runs in milliseconds and never depends on timing.
only has to show that the nodes find each other and that each heartbeat reaches the check.
